name: Roelof Botha

summary.text: Roelof Botha grew up in South Africa and is a grandson of former South African foreign minister Pik Botha. He studied actuarial science at the University of Cape Town (B.S. 1994), became a Fellow of the Faculty of Actuaries in 1996, and was a McKinsey consultant in South Africa from August 1996 to July 1998. While at Stanford Business School (MBA 2000) he was recruited by Elon Musk and joined the company in March 2000. He was VP of Financial & Risk Management, became CFO in August 2001, and led the 2002 IPO. In 2003 he joined Sequoia Capital, whose partner Michael Moritz sat on PayPal's board. No public record links him to Thiel, Hoffman, Sacks or Rabois before 2000, or to a government or intelligence role of his own.

facts.claim: Botha received a B.S. in Actuarial Science, Economics and Statistics from the University of Cape Town in 1994 and became a Fellow of the Faculty of Actuaries in 1996, according to PayPal's annual report. Some later profiles give 1996 as his graduation year.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Botha was a management consultant at McKinsey & Company from August 1996 to July 1998, in the firm's South African branch. A McKinsey colleague who was a Stanford GSB alumnus influenced his move to Stanford.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Botha said he joined the company in spring 2000, on a South African student visa, just after the X.com-Confinity merger. PayPal's filings date his arrival to March 2000.

facts.claim: Botha was 28 and listed as Chief Financial Officer in PayPal's February 2002 IPO registration statement, which also lists Michael Moritz and Elon Musk as directors.

facts.claim: In July 2001 PayPal lent Botha $112,500 under its non-recourse employee liquidity program. In September 2001 the company bought back part of participants' shares at $3 per share, and the proceeds repaid the loans.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Botha said Michael Moritz called to offer him a role at Sequoia, and he joined after PayPal's first earnings release in early 2003.
facts.quote: At that point I joined Sequoia.

facts.claim: Block's 2026 proxy statement says Botha has been with Sequoia Capital since 2003 and is now a Partner there. It also says that from 2000 to 2003 he held various positions at PayPal, including Chief Financial Officer.

sources.title: Block, Inc. - Form DEF 14A - FY2026

facts.claim: Botha led Sequoia's investment in YouTube and sat on its board before Google bought the 1.5-year-old company in 2006. Google announced on October 9, 2006 that it would acquire YouTube for $1.65 billion in a stock-for-stock transaction.

sources.title: Sequoia Capital's Roelof Botha is coming to Disrupt this fall
Press Release

facts.claim: Botha has been a Square/Block director since January 2011 and its Lead Independent Director since June 2022, sitting on its compensation and audit and risk committees. Block lists his current public company boards as Unity Software, Natera, MongoDB and Ethos Technologies. His past public boards were Eventbrite (October 2009 to June 2022), 23andMe (September 2017 to September 2024) and Bird Global (June 2018 to December 2022).

sources.title: Block, Inc. - Form DEF 14A - FY2026

facts.claim: In 2017 Botha was made head of Sequoia's U.S. business, working under Doug Leone. In April 2022 Sequoia announced he would replace Leone as 'Senior Steward' from July 5, 2022.

sources.title: Sequoia's Doug Leone steps down, making way for new global head Roelof Botha

facts.claim: In an October 2021 post, Botha announced that Sequoia was restructuring its U.S./Europe business around a single permanent fund. Limited partners would invest in The Sequoia Capital Fund, which would allocate money to closed-end sub-funds for each stage of venture investing and hold an open-ended liquid portfolio of public stakes in selected companies.
facts.quote: restructuring Sequoia Capital around a singular, permanent structure

facts.claim: An amended Schedule 13D in May 2022, during Botha's tenure as Sequoia's U.S. head, listed Sequoia as committing $800 million in equity to Elon Musk's $44 billion bid for Twitter. Other committed investors included VyCapital ($700 million), Binance ($500 million) and Andreessen Horowitz ($400 million).

sources.title: Sequoia, Binance and a16z back Elon Musk's $44 billion Twitter bid

facts.claim: In November 2022 Sequoia told its limited partners it had marked its FTX investments down to zero: $150 million held in Global Growth Fund III and $63.5 million in its SCGE public-equities fund, $213.5 million in total. The letter said that 'At the time of our investment in FTX, we ran a rigorous diligence process.'
facts.quote: At the time of our investment in FTX, we ran a rigorous diligence process.

sources.title: Sequoia says its investment in FTX is now worthless

facts.claim: In June 2023 Botha, Neil Shen and Shailendra Singh announced in a blog post and letter to limited partners that Sequoia would split into three firms by March 2024: Sequoia Capital (U.S./Europe), HongShan (China) and Peak XV Partners (India/Southeast Asia). The firm cited the complexity of a decentralized global business, brand confusion and portfolio conflicts. TechCrunch placed the split amid U.S.-China tension and proposed U.S. limits on investment in China.

sources.title: Sequoia splits China and India arms from US mothership to avoid 'portfolio conflict' and 'market confusion'

facts.claim: On September 17, 2024, Botha and the six other independent directors of 23andMe resigned together. In a letter to CEO Anne Wojcicki, they said she had not produced a 'fully financed, fully diligenced, actionable proposal' to take the company private, and that they differed with her on its strategic direction.

sources.title: EX-17 resignation letter

facts.claim: On November 4, 2025, Botha said he would step aside as Sequoia's steward and 'pass the baton' to Pat Grady and Alfred Lin. He moved into an advisory role while keeping the boards of companies he invested in. Fortune noted friction inside the firm over partner Shaun Maguire's posts about Zohran Mamdani; the FT reported that COO Sumaiya Balbale resigned over them. Botha said of Maguire: 'I think he has made it clear what he stands for.'

openQuestions: The brief names Deloitte as a prior employer. No source opened in this session supports a Deloitte role; the 10-K lists only McKinsey (1996-1998) before Stanford.
CFO start date differs by source: the 10-K says August 2001, while Wikipedia and secondary profiles say September 2001 or give 2000-2003.
Who introduced Botha to Musk is unconfirmed; secondary South African outlets (Daily Investor, BizNews summaries, not opened in full) say a mutual friend did.
No public record found of Botha holding a government or intelligence role, or of his family's political ties shaping his PayPal hiring or funding. The Pik Botha relationship is family only.
The Sequoia Crucible Moments page carries no reliable publication date (it rendered as the fetch date), so no date is given for that source.

FEC: an aggregator search result listed two $5,000 gifts (2021-11-19, 2022-09-15) from Botha (Sequoia) to committee C00150367, which FEC identifies as the National Venture Capital Association's VenturePAC. The gifts themselves were not verified because the FEC API was rate-limited. The same result listed a 2006 California state gift to the No on 82 (Reiner preschool initiative) campaign, also unverified.
Botha's personal role in the FTX diligence and investment decision is not documented in sources opened; Sequoia's letter speaks for the firm.
Botha's investment memo for YouTube and his declaration in Viacom v. YouTube (S.D.N.Y. 07-cv-2103, unsealed March 2010) are described only by blogs; primary docket not opened.

Secondary profiles credit Botha with leading Sequoia's April 2012 Instagram investment ($50M round at a $500M valuation, days before Facebook's ~$1B purchase); TechCrunch confirms Sequoia led the round but does not name Botha.
WSJ reportedly said partners asked Botha to step aside in 2025; not opened or verified.
Fortune (2025) dates his 'steward' role to 2017, while TechCrunch (2022) says he became U.S. head in 2017 and Senior Steward in July 2022; titles differ by source.
Botha has been quoted saying he is 'not a registered member of either party'; original source not located.
No post-2002 documented business ties to Peter Thiel found in sources opened.
